_comment: Committed metric baselines for the rb-eval regression gate. The harness FAILS if a quality metric drops below its baseline (with a 1e-9 tolerance). These were captured from a run over the committed fixtures with DeterministicProvider and reproduce bit-for-bit across runs. They guard ranking DETERMINISM and RELATIVE ORDERING (regression detection), not absolute semantic quality; see README.md. History: the W1.0a corpus expansion (12 -> 205 memories, 10 -> 72 natural-language goldens) reset recall@k to 0.0486 / mrr to 0.0518 -- the honest pre-Phase-1 starting line. W1.1+W1.7 (cosine metric + namespace partition) left recall@k unchanged and moved mrr to 0.0505 (noise-tie reshuffle). Re-captured for W1.2 (FTS tokenization): the keyword leg is ALIVE for natural-language queries (OR-of-individually-quoted-tokens replaces the whole-query phrase; porter stemming layered over unicode61 via migration 005), so the deterministic gate metrics jumped: recall@k 0.0486 -> 0.7847, mrr 0.0505 -> 0.9611 -- under non-semantic deterministic vectors the FTS channel is now the dominant useful signal, which is exactly the channel W1.2 revived (fts_query_rate 0.042 -> 1.0). dedup_precision moved 1.0 -> 0.9917: improved retrieval now co-ranks both members of some expected near-dup clusters in top-5, the legitimate trade the previous comment anticipated. The REAL-vector replay measurement vs docs/eval/2026-06-12-pre-phase1-baseline.json: golden recall@5 0.9213 -> 0.9630, mrr 0.9838 -> 0.9838 (flat), ndcg 0.9342 -> 0.9537, dedup 0.9306 -> 0.9472, fts_query_rate 0.0417 -> 1.0 (Phase 1 gate: >= 0.80). Versus the intermediate post-W1.1 state, replay mrr traded 0.9931 -> 0.9838 and ndcg 0.9558 -> 0.9537 for the recall/dedup/channel gains (full variant table in the escape_fts5_query decision record and the W1.2 commit body). Raising a baseline after an intentional ranking improvement, or lowering one for a justified trade-off, is a deliberate reviewed commit. Latency p50/p99 are reported but not gated (machine-dependent). Re-verified for W1.3 (score floor + empty state): the Linear recall floor SCORE_FLOOR=0.18 moved NO metric in any context -- deterministic gate recall@k/mrr/dedup bit-identical (the gate corpus is all-fresh, imp >= 5, so every returned result already scores >= 0.2253), and real-vector replay goldens (0.9630/0.9838/0.9537/0.9472) and holdout (0.9750/0.9500/0.9498/0.9700) are bit-identical with the floor on vs off -- the floor only trims below-floor tail junk (positions past the metric horizon). Derivation arithmetic lives on rb_search::SCORE_FLOOR; the sweep tool is rb-eval/tests/score_floor_diag.rs. Re-captured for W1.4 (query-kind embeddings): NO metric moved -- DeterministicProvider is kind-blind by design (embed_query == embed_document, pinned by test), so the deterministic gate is bit-identical (0.7847/0.9611/0.9917), and the committed all-MiniLM-L6-v2 replay fixture serves query-kind lookups via the document-kind fallback (byte-identical vectors for this kind-blind model), so replay goldens (0.9630/0.9838/0.9537/0.9472) and holdout (0.9750/0.9500/0.9498) are bit-identical too. The semantic effect of input_type=query lands only when a Voyage fixture is recorded (key required; deferred).
